title: Pozole Rojo Red Hominy Soup

seo.title: Pozole Rojo Recipe: Authentic Mexican Red Hominy Soup
seo.metaDescription: Learn how to make the best authentic Pozole Rojo recipe at home! This hearty Mexican red hominy soup is perfect for any occasion. Get the full step-by-step guide.

seo.imageCaption: Warm up with a comforting bowl of homemade Pozole Rojo, a traditional Mexican red hominy soup.

description: Experience the rich, comforting flavors of traditional Pozole Rojo, a beloved Mexican red hominy soup. This hearty stew features tender pork simmered in a vibrant, savory broth made from dried chiles, perfect for celebrations or a cozy family meal. Garnished with fresh toppings, it is a truly satisfying dish that embodies the soul of Mexican cuisine.

instructions.title: Cook the Pork
instructions.text: Place the pork shoulder, one half of the onion, 3 garlic cloves, and 1 teaspoon of salt in a large pot. Cover with water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until the pork is very tender. Skim off any foam that rises to the surface. Once cooked, remove the pork, shred it, and set aside. Strain the cooking liquid and reserve for the soup.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chile Sauce
instructions.text: While the pork cooks, rehydrate the dried guajillo and ancho chiles. Place them in a bowl, cover with hot water, and let them soak for 20-30 minutes until soft. Drain the chiles, reserving some soaking liquid. In a blender, combine the rehydrated chiles, the remaining 3 garlic cloves, the other half of the onion, oregano, cumin, and 1/2 cup of the chile soaking liquid or chicken broth. Blend until very smooth. If needed, add more liquid a tablespoon at a time to achieve a smooth consistency.

instructions.title: Sear the Pork and Strain the Sauce
instructions.text: In a clean large pot, add a tablespoon of oil and sear the shredded pork until lightly browned. This adds depth of flavor. Carefully pour the blended chile sauce through a fine-mesh sieve directly into the pot with the pork, pressing on the solids to extract all the liquid. Discard the remaining pulp.

instructions.title: Combine and Simmer
instructions.text: Add the reserved pork cooking liquid and the 8 cups of chicken broth to the pot with the pork and strained chile sauce. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low. Add the drained and rinsed hominy. Stir well, cover, and let it simmer for at least 30 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. The longer it simmers, the richer the flavor.

instructions.title: Season and Adjust
instructions.text: Taste the pozole and adjust seasoning with salt as needed. If the soup is too thick, you can add a little more broth or water. Ensure the hominy is tender and the pork is well integrated into the broth.

instructions.title: Serve with Garnishes
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Pozole Rojo into individual bowls. Serve immediately with a variety of fresh garnishes on the side, allowing each person to customize their bowl. Essential garnishes include shredded cabbage, thinly sliced radishes, diced white onion, fresh cilantro, and lime wedges for squeezing.

tips: For a deeper flavor, toast the dried chiles lightly in a dry pan for a minute or two before rehydrating them. Be careful not to burn them.
Do not skip straining the chile sauce. This step is crucial for achieving a smooth, velvety broth characteristic of authentic pozole, free from fibrous bits.
Pozole tastes even better the next day! Make it ahead of time and refrigerate. Reheat gently on the stovetop, adding a splash of broth or water if it has thickened too much.
